headline: URANIUM FACES STRUCTURAL DEFICIT AS AI DATA CENTRES IGNITE UNPRECEDENTED NUCLEAR DEMAND
snippet: Nuclear reactor builds are now outpacing new uranium mine supply as AI data centres and cloud computing drive a step-change in baseload power demand; long-term uranium closed September at $96.50/lb, above its 2007 peak, while spot sits at $89.63.

headline: AUSTRALIA REVAMPS RARE EARTH REFINING POLICY — ARAFURA SURGES 10%+ ON NOLANS PROJECT TAILWIND
snippet: The Australian federal government overhauled its rare earth refinery support framework, boosting domestic processing incentives; Arafura Rare Earths (ASX: ARU) led ASX rare earth stocks sharply higher as improved policy certainty strengthened the economics of its Nolans project in the Northern Territory.

headline: BHP HALTS ESCONDIDA — WORLD'S BIGGEST COPPER MINE — AFTER WORKER FATALITY
snippet: BHP Group (ASX: BHP) suspended operations at Escondida in Chile following a worker's death; the mine accounts for roughly 5% of global copper supply, and the halt adds a new supply-side variable as LME copper trades within striking distance of its September record high.

headline: COPPER BOUNCES 1.7% TO $6.72/LB AS AI STOCKS RECOVER AND CHINESE PHYSICAL DEMAND FIRMS
snippet: LME copper climbed 1.7% to US$6.72/lb overnight as a recovery in AI-related equities lifted risk sentiment and Chinese physical buyers stepped in; copper equities on the ASX followed the metal higher, with the rally stacking on top of Tuesday's Yangshan import premium already at multi-year highs.

headline: WHITE CLIFF HITS 11.5M AT 2.00% Cu IN MAIDEN BORNITE HILLS DRILL — PEAK OF 16.3% IN NUNAVUT
snippet: White Cliff Minerals (ASX: WCN) returned 11.5m at 2.00% copper including a 16.3% peak intercept in maiden drilling at the Bornite Hills target of its Rae copper project in Nunavut, Canada; the result opens a new high-priority drill target on the project.

headline: WEST AFRICAN RESOURCES POSTS RECORD QUARTER — SANBRADO AND KIAKA HOLD ABOVE 500,000oz RUN RATE
snippet: West African Resources (ASX: WAF) delivered another record third quarter from its Sanbrado and Kiaka operations in Burkina Faso, maintaining an annualised run rate above 500,000 gold ounces; the All Ords Gold index rose 3.3% on Wednesday as spot gold recovered 1.1% overnight.

headline: GLOBAL ENERGY METALS FLAGS MULTIPLE URANIUM TARGETS AT CHARLOT-NEELY LAKE, SASKATCHEWAN
snippet: Global Energy Metals Corp. highlighted new uranium drill targets at its Charlot-Neely Lake project in Saskatchewan's Athabasca Basin corridor; the company cited accelerating electrification and critical battery metal demand as drivers for advancing the project.

headline: INVENTUS MINING WRAPS 89-HOLE PARDO PHASE 2 NEAR SUDBURY — MAIDEN RESOURCE ESTIMATE AHEAD
snippet: Inventus Mining (TSXV: IVS) completed its Phase 2 program at the Pardo "River of Gold" project 65km northeast of Sudbury, Ontario, with 89 final holes assayed; highlights include 4.47 g/t Au over 2.19m in the shallow Main Layer, and a maiden resource estimate is in preparation.

headline: RARE EARTH STOCKS SLIP 3-5% DAY AFTER TUESDAY'S 11% SURGE — USAR AND MP MATERIALS LEAD DECLINE
snippet: USA Rare Earth (USAR) and MP Materials (MP) each fell 5% on Wednesday, reversing part of Tuesday's 11% pop; the sector remains volatile as going-concern warnings and sharp year-to-date losses keep investors cautious despite the brief policy-driven rallies.

headline: CPM GROUP: GOLD AND SILVER RALLY IS NEAR — BUT FURTHER DOWNSIDE REMAINS POSSIBLE BEFORE THE TURN
snippet: CPM Group issued a precious metals alert saying the next rally is drawing close as gold consolidates near $4,000 support with silver within 2% of its 2026 yearly low, but cautioned that additional selling pressure is still possible before the cycle turns higher.

headline: AGNICO EAGLE, KINROSS AND ALAMOS REPORT TONIGHT AS GOLD EARNINGS SEASON HITS ITS PEAK
snippet: Three senior gold producers — Agnico Eagle, Kinross and Alamos Gold — report after the close on October 28; rising energy costs with Brent crude above $116/bbl and gold's 4.1% weekly decline are the main themes to watch after Newmont's record Q3 result was met with a 4.6% stock drop.

headline: WEST WITS MINING DRILLS 5,750m AT BIRD REEF CENTRAL URANIUM-GOLD PROJECT IN SOUTH AFRICA
snippet: West Wits Mining (ASX: WWI) commissioned a 17-hole, 5,750m diamond drill program at its Bird Reef Central uranium-gold project in South Africa, targeting a zone with dual exposure to uranium above $89/lb spot and gold holding above $4,000/oz.
